facts.text: Capital project report of the Project Planning Committee for the University of Toronto Emerging and Pandemic Infections Centre (EPIC) facility, agenda item 3(c). Report date March 15, 2022 for the March 22, 2022 Executive Committee.
Committee of Adjustment approved a minor height variance (final and binding letter dated December 22, 2021). This is a zoning matter, separate from building-code items.
The Medical Sciences Building is 'earmarked for future designation'. Heritage Preservation Services will review and approve administratively through the building permit submitted December 23, 2021.
'An Alternative Solution package will be submitted to the City January 12, 2022, to get approval for use of flammables below grade.'
Schedule assumption in a footnote: 'City of Toronto accepts Alternative solution'.

The EPIC3 lab 'cannot be designed for universal accessibility'. Autoclave decontamination of wheelchairs and other mobility devices, and strict emergency and evacuation procedures, are described as challenges for people with disabilities.

Consultants are to ensure that restricted access complies with the Building Code and Fire Code. For areas other than the EPIC3 lab, a Universal Design Consultant 'typically will be retained' early in the design process.
The report notes the Ontario Building Code accessibility amendment filed December 27, 2013 (O. Reg. 368/13), effective for applications after January 1, 2015, with more stringent requirements.
